v.rationale: All three share the same batch design: a job inside the batch adds the per-account jobs, allowFailures, a dedicated statements queue and a finally step. The deciding factor was whether the failure count stays accurate when a job dies outside its own try/catch, for example on a worker timeout. A probe that fails the last statement job through $job->fail() showed impl-1 correct (uses $batch->failedJobs), impl-3 inconsistent (failed()=1 but status completed and a summary saying 0 failed, because failed() runs after the batch has finalised) and impl-2 plainly wrong (completed, 0 failed). impl-1 also writes the PDF safely on retry and has the strongest tests on a real database queue. Its main defects are duplicate emails if the fan-out job is retried and counting a deleted account as a success. impl-3 is modern and clean but has the ordering bug and the same retry-duplication risk. impl-2 is the simplest but uses string constants, sets no timeouts, and silently loses failures and possibly accounts. None of the three prunes job_batches.
